# netgear_lag (Data Source)

One link aggregation group, read from `show running-config`.

The switch defines every LAG interface whether or not it is used, but only groups that carry configuration appear in the running config. Reading one that does not is an error.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "netgear_lag" "uplink" {
  lag_id = 1
}

# Put the group in a VLAN by referencing the interface id the switch gives it.
resource "netgear_vlan" "mgmt" {
  vlan_id      = 10
  tagged_ports = [data.netgear_lag.uplink.interface_id]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `lag_id` (Number) LAG number to look up. The GS724Tv4 defines 1 through 26.

### Read-Only

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the LAG is administratively up.
- `hash_mode` (Number) Load balance selector. Zero when the group is left at the switch default.
- `id` (String) The LAG id as a string.
- `interface_id` (String) The LAG's interface id, such as `3/1`. Use this where other resources expect a port.
- `members` (Set of String) Physical ports in the bundle, in FASTPATH notation such as `0/1`.
- `mode` (String) `lacp` for 802.3ad negotiation, or `static` for an unconditional bundle.
- `name` (String) LAG name, empty when the switch has none for it.
